Exclusion refusals return 400. These describe input-validation behavior only and add no trust grant or wire field. No change to A-001 confidentiality or TB-002 encryption was identified.

Bridge, head 153-157: native-tracked engines now refuse requests with logprobs or token constraints before admission, as typed unsupportedOutputControl client errors. The refusal finalizes the prefix-cache lookup signal with .policy and finishes the continuation. Head 96-101 maps the thrown error to a nonthrowing error stream, mirroring the existing handling. This narrows behavior: it is a fail-closed refusal with no plaintext emission (T-008) and no new attack surface. It reduces spurious coordinator breaker strikes, which is an availability improvement.

(2) Confirm that the error string is mapped to the closed invalid_request/client_error vocabulary, i.e. that the unsupportedOutputControlPrefix marker mapping exists in unchanged code.
(3) The submodule bump 7bed821…→6aef0a5… changes the native inference engine (TB-007) without visible diff. It may alter EngineV2.validateRequest, KV/prefix-cache handling (T-041, T-028), or nativeShutdownExecutionContractID semantics. It is an unverified coverage gap that needs upstream diff review.
